findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed that the heat dish machine was not reaching a high enough surface temperature to effectively sanitize equipment. The final temperature measuring device measured a surface temperature of 148 F, when 160 F is required for sanitizing. A final temperature sticker also confirmed a temperature of less than 160 F. The PIC was notified and all dishes will instead be warewashed in the cafeteria facilities in another part of the building until the heat dish machine is repaired. Ensure that hot water warewashing reaches a utensil surface temperature of at least 160 F to effectively sanitize equipment
findings.citation_text: 4-703.11(B) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (B) Hot water mechanical operations by being cycled through EQUIPMENT that is set up as specified under §§ 4-501.15, 4-501.112, and 4-501.113 and achieving a UTENSIL surface temperature of 71°C (160°F) as measured by an irreversible registering temperature indicator. [P]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee used their barehand to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The employee was educated about the proper hand washing procedure when the action was observed. Ensure that employees always use a barrier to turn off the faucet to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Inspector observed that there were three wiping cloths sitting on countertops throughout the facility. No sanitizer bucket was prepared to store the wiping cloths in. Ensure that in-use wiping cloths are stored in sanitizer solution if they are wet. Clean, dry wiping cloths may sit on surfaces. Person in charge instructed operator to make sanitizer and place the cloths in the buckets once the sanitizer is made. Corrected on site. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
Ice scoop was observed to be sitting handle down in the ice bin. The handle of utensils must never be in contact with food. Company policy is to leave scoops outside of the ice in a holder. Ensure that scoops are stored outside of the ice to prevent contamination. The ice scoop was removed from the bin and stored in the appropriate container during the inspection. Corrected on site. 

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: Upon arrival, inspector did not observe any sanitizer buckets in use during operations. Operator at the facility explained that one had not been made as of yet. Operator was instructed by person in charge to make up a sanitizer bucket during the inspection. Sanitizer was made available immediately. Corrected on site.
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. 
(B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment: 5-205.11: (A) Observed an employee dump coffee into hand sink in food prep area. A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.
